topic: Fact-check of 'M2 MacBook Air rendering ceiling, and AI-agent workflow efficiency' (checked 23 Sep 2026; web search budget was exhausted, so all checks used direct fetches of primary sources, GitHub, PyPI and npm)

checks.claim: Model MC7X4 is the 13-inch M2 MacBook Air with 16 GB and 256 GB, so the owner very probably has the 8-core GPU and a 256 GB SSD.
checks.correction: This is stronger than the report's 'from memory'. A Best Buy product record gives Model Number MC7X4LL/A: 'MacBook Air 13-inch – Apple M2 – 16GB Memory – 256GB SSD', Graphics 'Apple M2 8-core', Midnight. Flipkart and Kaspi scrapes agree on 16 GB / 256 GB. The owner should still confirm with system_profiler.

checks.claim: Apple's Metal Feature Set Tables (21 May 2026) put M2 in family Apple8 with Metal 3 and 4 support. By family: mesh shading needs Apple7, MetalFX spatial upscaling Apple3, temporal upscaling Apple7, frame interpolation Apple5 and denoised upscaling Apple9. M5 is Apple10, and the largest 2D texture is 16384. Hardware ray-traversal first appears in family 9 (M3).
checks.correction: Every row matches the PDF, dated 21 May 2026. On M2, Metal ray tracing is available only on the general shader cores; the table lists 'Ray tracing in compute pipelines' from Apple6. Apple's M3 tech talk (developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/111375) confirms that hardware-accelerated ray tracing and mesh shading are new in family 9. Caution: WebFetch's own summary of this PDF invented a different table. Read the raw text.

checks.claim: WWDC20 'Optimize Metal Performance for Apple silicon Macs': alpha-tested foliage produces 'feedback' fragments that reduce the benefit of hidden-surface removal. Draw opaque, then feedback, then translucent. Load and store actions consume 'the majority of your app's system bandwidth'.
checks.correction: The transcript quotes match word for word.

checks.claim: The 10-core M2 GPU runs at 1.398 GHz for 3,579 GFLOPS FP32, which scales to about 2.86 TFLOPS for 8 cores. Memory bandwidth is 100 GB/s. The recommended GPU working set is about two-thirds of RAM (listed as unverified).
checks.correction: The metal-benchmarks table row reads 'M2 | 8 | 1.398 | 10 | 3579'. The llama.cpp table gives M2 as 100 GB/s. The working-set figure can now be marked verified: ggml Metal logs on a 16 GB Apple8 device (M2 Pro) report recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize = 11453.25 MB, which is 10,922.67 MiB and exactly two-thirds of 16 GiB (github.com/01-ai/Yi README). Plan for about 10.7 GiB of GPU-visible memory at most, before macOS and browser overhead.

checks.claim: Latest Godot versions are 4.7.2 stable (18 Aug 2026) and 4.8-dev6 (15 Sep 2026). Godot uses MetalFX temporal upscaling from 4.4 onwards.
checks.correction: git tags and the godot-builds release pages confirm both dates. The 4.4-stable source already has MFXSpatialEffect and MFXTemporalEffect (MTLFXTemporalScaler). I did not verify the 170.6 MB macOS editor zip size, because the asset list failed to load.

checks.claim: Godot's --headless mode uses the headless display driver and the dummy audio driver; frame capture needs --write-movie with --fixed-fps and --quit-after. Issue #82435 (Forward+ and Mobile crash on llvmpipe/lavapipe; Compatibility works) is still open and labelled confirmed.
checks.correction: The docs define --headless as '--display-driver headless --audio-driver Dummy'. --write-movie forces --fixed-fps, and --quit-after sets the frame count. #82435 is open with the labels bug, confirmed, crash and topic:rendering. Correction: mesa-vulkan-drivers 25.2.8-0ubuntu0.24.04.2 is already installed in this container, not just installable. Whether Forward+ runs on lavapipe in 4.7 or 4.8 is still unproven.

checks.claim: Godot issue #119436 reports a Metal 'timeout waiting for fence' freeze on an M2 MacBook Air with Godot 4.6.1.
checks.correction: The issue is open and labelled confirmed on 4.6.1, but it is not specific to the M2 Air. It also reproduces on an M1 Max and an M4-series Mac. It is assigned to the Metal driver maintainer, and the reporter says they have a patch. Treat it as a general Godot Metal risk, not an M2 Air limitation.

checks.claim: PyPI publishes official bpy wheels: 5.2.2 (15 Sep 2026, Python 3.13, manylinux x86_64 and macOS arm64, about 400 MB) and LTS 4.5.14 (15 Sep 2026, Python 3.11). mcp-for-blender is at 2.0.0 (16 Sep 2026).
checks.correction: The bpy facts are correct. 5.2.2 requires Python ==3.13.* exactly. The Linux wheel is 402 MB and the macOS arm64 wheel 245 MB. The container's default python3 is 3.11, although /usr/bin/python3.13 exists, so agents must create a 3.13 virtual environment or use 4.5.14 (cp311). mcp-for-blender's latest release is 2.0.3 (21 Sep 2026), not 2.0.0 (pypi.org/project/mcp-for-blender).

checks.claim: Agent-cost figures: multi-agent systems use about 15× the tokens of chat and agents about 4×; agent teams about 7× a standard session; the enterprise average is about $13 per developer per active day; CLI tools are preferred over MCP; CLAUDE.md should stay under 200 lines. Image cost is ⌈w/28⌉×⌈h/28⌉ visual tokens (1280x800 ≈ 1,334), capped at 2576 px / 4,784 tokens on newer models.
checks.correction: The costs page confirms the 7×, $13, 'Prefer CLI tools' and under-200-lines figures. The Anthropic engineering post confirms '4× … 15× more tokens than chats'. The vision docs confirm the formula, and the 2576 px / 4,784 tier applies to 'Claude 4.7 and later models'. The docs also say base64 images are re-sent on every turn and recommend the Files API.

checks.claim: GitHub Free/Pro Git LFS includes 10 GiB storage and 10 GiB bandwidth, and the largest LFS file is 2 GiB. Each release asset must be under 2 GiB, and there is no limit on total release size or bandwidth.
checks.correction: Confirmed by large_files.yml and about-releases.md. Omitted limit: at most 1,000 assets per release (data/variables/releases.yml).

checks.claim: The fanless M2 Air loses a significant share of GPU performance under sustained load (no figure given).
checks.correction: The egress proxy blocks review sites (notebookcheck, anandtech, tomshardware), apple.com and Wikipedia, and web search was exhausted. No primary measurement was found, so the 10-minute warm benchmark on the owner's Mac stays the only acceptance evidence. The UK Mac prices are also unverifiable here.

important_omissions: WebGPU support on the owner's Mac. Safari 26 (released 15 Sep 2025; runs on macOS Sonoma, Sequoia and Tahoe) added WebGPU, and Chrome has had it on macOS since version 113. Safari 26 lacks two things this plan needs: GPU timestamp queries, which a browser-route benchmark needs for per-pass GPU timings, and 'transient' (memoryless) attachments, which Apple's advice on load/store bandwidth relies on. Chrome has timestamp queries (fully from 144) and transient attachments (146+). Any three.js/Babylon/PlayCanvas benchmark on the Mac should therefore run in Chrome. Sources: @mdn/browser-compat-data 8.1.2 on npm (api.GPUQuerySet timestamp, createTexture accept_transient_attachment); Safari 26 release notes at developer.apple.com/documentation/safari-release-notes/safari-26-release-notes.

The headless-render proof is weaker than the report implies. docs/engine_selection/RESUME.md (branch claude/aokigahara-engine-selection-tqyqx6) says the 0.65 s and 1.8 s per frame SwiftShader WebGPU timings were on placeholder geometry, in Chromium 141 ('1194' is Playwright's build number). Cloud audit time for a real frame with 2–4 M triangles, dense alpha foliage, shadow cascades and SSGI on 4 CPUs is unmeasured and could be minutes per frame. That changes how many audit renders the loop can afford.
The bpy 5.2.2 wheel requires Python 3.13 exactly, while the container's default is 3.11. Cloud baking scripts must pin a 3.13 virtual environment or use LTS 4.5.14 (pypi.org/pypi/bpy/json).

Lavapipe (Mesa 25.2.8) is already installed in the container, so the Godot Forward+ plus Xvfb headless test (#82435) costs almost nothing to run. It should be run before the engine decision rather than left as 'unverified'.
The Godot Metal fence freeze (#119436) is still open on 4.6.1 and affects several Apple Silicon Macs. Whether 4.7.x includes the fix is not established. This matters if Godot is chosen for the M2.
overall_reliability: High for the claims the engine decision rests on. The SKU and 8-core GPU, the Metal feature table, no hardware ray tracing on M2, the HSR and alpha-foliage guidance, FLOPS and bandwidth, the Godot versions and MetalFX, the headless and lavapipe status, bpy availability, the token-cost figures and the GitHub LFS and release limits all checked out against primary sources, and none were refuted. Minor corrections: #119436 is not specific to the M2 Air, mcp-for-blender is now 2.0.3, and bpy 5.2.2 is pinned to Python 3.13. The performance budgets (2–4 M triangles, 30 fps at about 1 MP, per-effect ms), the throttling magnitude, UK prices and the single-NAND SSD point remain the author's unverified estimates. Treat them as hypotheses for the warm benchmark on the Mac, not as evidence.
